titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 40: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 40. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: The framed manuscript page number ⲙ (top left) is printed with a bar above and below as the frame, not as a supralinear stroke. Strokes over ⲛ of ⲛⲧⲁⲣⲉ (493–505), ⲛ of ⲛⲧⲉ (984–997) and the final ⲙ (1173–1187); the stroke over ϩ of ⲡⲱⲛϩ is printed obliquely (804–816); no stroke over ⲙⲛ or over ϩ of ⲛⲉⲧⲁⲛϩ.
Stroke over ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲓⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ (566–579); the stroke over the final ⲧ of ⲛⲟⲩⲱϣⲧ is printed obliquely (843–857, 8×).
Strokes over ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲟⲟⲩⲉ (608–622) and ⲛ of ϩⲛ (741–753). Dot under the final ⲡ of ⲉⲧϣⲟⲟⲡ.
A wide blank (106 px, measured in the x-height band), not marked by the editors, stands before the enlarged ⲧ of ⲧⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲧⲉ.
Strokes over ⲛ of ⲛⲟⲩⲧⲁⲓⲟ (666–678) and the final ⲛ (1203–1215).

Measured overline over ⲡⲛⲁ (934–979, pixel row): the first ⲡ of ⲡⲡⲛⲁ is not covered; second ⲡ 93 %, ⲛ 100 %, ⲁ 83 %. The stroke over ϩ of ⲉⲧⲁⲛϩ is printed obliquely (1075–1087); stroke over the free-standing ⲛ (1110–1124).

Measured stroke over ϩⲙ (697–721, pixel row): ϩ 46 %, ⲙ 68 %, encoded on ⲙ only. Measured stroke over the final ⲛⲛ (1160–1178): first ⲛ 47 %, second ⲛ 60 %, encoded on the second only; the second ⲛ also carries a sublinear dot.

Measured stroke over ϩⲛ (1110–1129, pixel row): ϩ 43 %, ⲛ 60 %, encoded on ⲛ only. Stroke over the first ⲛ of ⲛⲛⲁϭ (1158–1171). The dot under ϯ of ⲁϥϯⲙⲧⲁⲛ sits below the stem, apart from it (x 939, 8×).

Stroke over ⲛ of ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ (638–651).
"leer" after ⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ → vac.
Stroke over ⲛ of ⲛⲧⲁⲅⲁ (1201–1215). The dot under ⲓ of ϣⲁϥϫⲓ is a sublinear dot (x 997).
The edition opens a bracket before ⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ and prints twelve dots after it (x 921–1211) with no closing bracket; the letters and dots go into the restoration, closed at the line end (as 28.31).
Measured stroke over ⲛϥ of ⲛϥⲣ (555–572, pixel row): ⲛ 50 %, ϥ 62 %, encoded on both; a separate stroke over ⲣ (581–592).
All ϣ on the page were checked in the lower-zone sheets (ll. 3, 4, 6, 12, 13, 15, 17, 18, 20, 22, 23, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 33, 34); none is dotted.
